A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SafeConstellations and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Matching relocated material and inspecting the figures supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original model evaluations, steering ablations, MMLU results, representation analyses, and latency measurements.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results in its main text and appendices.

M1.justification: Task-specific centroids, confidence gating, dynamic layer selection, adaptive steering intensity, and the inference procedure remain unchanged. Specifying the final input token clarifies the representation being extracted; it does not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same five-task benchmark drawn from Alpaca, XSTest, JailbreakBench, SaladBench, and custom RAG-QA data, alongside MMLU. No dataset, language, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the same unsteered LLaMA and Qwen references and steering variants. The model-family comparisons also remain unchanged. Newly cited representation-steering research is not added as an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Both report the same 75/25 stratified split, 270-example test evaluation, model configurations, GPT-4o judging protocols, and MMLU subset evaluation. No changed preprocessing, metric, budget, or testing procedure is documented.

E4.justification: The component ablations, trajectory and cluster-separation analyses, qualitative failure cases, and latency/scalability analyses are retained. The quantitative discussion in v4 Section 6 largely comes from v2 Appendix A.3.2, rather than introducing a new analysis.

E5.justification: Both specify random seed 42 for all experiments and retain the same latency-distribution reporting. Moving the cluster-separation analysis into the main text introduces no repeated-run information, confidence intervals, or significance testing.

E6.justification: Table 2 retains LLaMA's 4.81% over-refusal rate, 72.92% reduction, and 46.57% MMLU score, alongside Qwen's 2.96%, 63.64%, and 28.42%. Task-specific results, silhouette scores, and qualitative examples also match. The reformatted latency plot shows the same data; the other figure images are identical.

T1.justification: Equations 1–10 and the appendix layer-effectiveness formula retain the same mathematical content. No substantive definition, assumption, derivation, theorem, or proof is introduced or revised.

C1.justification: v4 drops the abstract's quantified 'up to 73%' headline, although the result remains in Table 2. Its conclusion recasts safety preservation from appropriate caution on genuinely harmful inputs to preserving refusals to generic harmful inputs. The benchmark and task-conditioned steering contributions remain.

C2.justification: The new Ethical Considerations section explains steering misuse risks and assigns developers responsibility for defining benign tasks. Conversely, v4 removes the explicit limitation concerning LLM-judge bias or drift affecting metrics and steering targets, together with the recommendation for human validation. The batch-steering limitation is relocated from the appendix.

D1.justification: Footnote 1 changes the dataset access link from GitHub to Hugging Face and replaces the commit-specific code link with the repository root, removing the revision pin. Existing judge prompts, hyperparameters, hardware disclosures, and memory details remain. These are documented access changes; external availability was not checked.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the references add Arditi et al. (2024) on single-direction refusal and mechanistic-interpretability surveys by Naseem (2026) and Zhang et al. (2026). The broader positioning against task-agnostic mitigation remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 introduces a Discussion section grouping existing analyses, reorganizes appendix subsections, separates Limitations from the conclusion, and adds Ethical Considerations. It also edits wording and corrects appendix references. Most introductory, methodological, and experimental prose is retained.

P2.justification: The qualitative table, cluster-separation figure and table, and latency figure move from the appendix into the main text. The latency panels change from stacked to side-by-side, judge prompts receive new box styling, and the final-page trajectory plots are enlarged. Most displays retain their original graphics and structure.

improvement.justification: v4 makes existing validation and failure examples easier to find, corrects cross-references, and adds a concrete misuse discussion. However, it removes the judge-bias and human-validation caveat and drops the code revision pin. With the scientific evidence unchanged, these gains in exposition and risk discussion coexist with losses in transparency and reproducibility specificity, without a reliably clear net quality direction.
